# temps_wireguard_mesh (Resource)

Turns on the encrypted WireGuard mesh between the nodes of the cluster. Temps refuses while `can_enable` is false; `enable_blocker` says why. Temps has no endpoint to turn the mesh off, so destroying the resource only stops managing it.

Import with `wireguard_mesh`.

Required API key permissions: `settings:read`, `settings:write`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "temps_wireguard_mesh" "this" {
  cidr        = "10.100.0.0/24"
  listen_port = 51820
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `cidr` (String) Address range of the mesh.
- `listen_port` (Number) UDP port WireGuard listens on.
- `node_api_port` (Number) Port of the node API over the mesh. Temps never returns it, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected.

### Read-Only

- `can_enable` (Boolean) Whether the mesh can be turned on.
- `enable_blocker` (String) What prevents turning it on.
- `id` (String) Import ID, `wireguard_mesh`.
- `state` (String) Mesh state.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Singleton: the import ID is the resource type without the prefix.
terraform import temps_wireguard_mesh.this wireguard_mesh
```
